summary_md:
**[@sakikoazu](https://x.com/sakikoazu/status/2115051410761081208)** summarizes **DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration** — only the *main* agent is trained to write its own multi-agent workflows while sub-agents stay frozen. With Qwen3.5-27B it reaches ~88% overall across six benchmarks vs ~77% for the best baseline, and it chooses to skip workflows entirely on about 47% of questions.

In a [follow-up](https://x.com/sakikoazu/status/2115051556500550025) they add (having read but not run it) that the *untrained* base model does worse with forced workflows than answering directly on most math sets — training is what makes collaboration pay — and note caveats: only 688 questions, and GPQA still trails Self-Refine.
relevance: Learned, selective orchestration (knowing when *not* to spawn agents) is a key cognition skill for agent systems.
